flagged.title: Nature & Spiritual Belonging
flagged.reason: The video presents an entirely incorrect analysis of Landon's poem (claiming the siblings are physically separated by global exploration and bridged by sea and sky) and misinterprets Brontë's poem regarding the family home.

mark_affecting.quote: Even though her brother is sailing halfway across the globe, she knows they're looking at the exact same sky, they're feeling the exact same wind. Nature is the medium that keeps this brother and sister anchored to one another
Landon | Nature: Bridge | Form: Flowing | Context: Exploration
proving that a sense of belonging really can stretch all the way across the globe.
Then we move through the Age of Exploration with Landon, where the world suddenly gets a whole lot bigger, and nature becomes a way to actually manage that distance.

For Brontë, belonging isn't about sitting in a cozy living room with a bunch of people. Not at all. Belonging is about being out on those windswept moors and being totally absorbed into this sublime natural world.

flagged.reason: F14 is mark-affecting because claiming the poem 'Us' examines Urdu and his father's Kashmiri roots misrepresents the content of the set text, which would penalise a student's AO1 textual understanding in an exam.

mark_affecting.quote: he uses the word 'us' to examine the gap between his father's Kashmiri roots and his own English upbringing [...] It's the linguistic borderland between English and Urdu.
